previous.speaker: Eric Sunshine
previous.quote:
The actual diffs output by range-diff respect diff_option.file, which
range-diff passes down the call-chain, thus are destination-agnostic.
However, output_pair_header() is hard-coded to emit to 'stdout'. Fix
this by making output_pair_header() respect diff_option.file, as well.

incoming.speaker: Ævar Arnfjörð Bjarmason
incoming.quote:
In 73a834e9e2 ("range-diff: relieve callers of low-level configuration
burden", 2018-07-22) we broke passing down options like --no-patch,
--stat etc.

Fix that regression, and add a test asserting the pre-73a834e9e2
behavior for some of these diff options.

alternative.speaker: Fabian Stelzer
alternative.quote:
When running the full test suite many tests can be skipped because of
missing prerequisites. It not easy right now to get an overview of which
ones are missing.
When switching to a new machine or environment some libraries and tools
might be missing or maybe a dependency broke completely. In this case
the tests would indicate nothing since all dependant tests are simply
skipped. This could hide broken behaviour or missing features in the
build. Therefore this patch summarizes the missing prereqs at the end of
the test run making it easier to spot such cases.

report_anchor.speaker: Phillip Wood
report_anchor.quote:
As the address sanitizer checks for a superset of the issues detected
by setting MALLOC_CHECK_ (which tries to detect things like double
frees and off-by-one errors) there is no need to set the latter when
compiling with -fsanitize=address.

previous.speaker: Junio C Hamano
previous.quote:
Essentially, this makes unpack_*() functions that are asked to
unpack a loose object header to be a bit more strict and detect an
input that cannot possibly be a valid object header, even before the
parsing function kicks in.

incoming.speaker: Ævar Arnfjörð Bjarmason
incoming.quote:
In practice this regression in v2.34.0 caused us to claim that we
couldn't parse the header, as opposed to not being able to unpack
it. Before the change in the C code the test_cmp added here would emit:

	-error: unable to unpack header of ./objects/e6/[ref]
	+error: unable to parse header of ./objects/e6/[ref]
